address_spaces.name: cached
address_spaces.notes: The cached xkphys base, with no attribute; the same value as the Origin 200.

address_spaces.name: Hub special
address_spaces.notes: Attribute 0, as on the Origin 200. Split on IP35 into a 128 MB local register window at 0x1000_0000 and a 128 MB boot window at 0x1800_0000, with remote forms at 0x3000_0000 and 0x3800_0000. The L1 UART is inside the register window. The OpenBSD board-identification read remains an unresolved consumer requirement.

address_spaces.name: I/O
address_spaces.notes: 16 MB small windows at widget times 16 MB; 512 MB big windows in M mode at (entry plus one) times 512 MB, selected by seven translation entries; the Bedrock's own registers are widget 1 of the node.

address_spaces.name: uncached memory
address_spaces.notes: Attribute 3. The node number sits at physical bits 39:33 in M mode, seven bits, an 8 GB node window and 128 nodes; N mode halves the window and is out of scope.

components.description: The tall rack that holds the whole system.
components.name: Origin 3400 tall rack
sources: 007-4311-002 printed page 89, Appendix B: an Origin 3400 has one to eight four-processor C-bricks, at least one I-brick and at most eight I/O bricks, at most two R-bricks, in a tall rack

components.name: R-brick
components.notes: The L1 brick-type character is not set: no reviewed L1 contract gives the R-brick's. The rear L1 PORT, which carries the USB hub's upstream link to the rack's L2, the two fans and the power board's +48 Vdc domain are not modelled.
sources: 007-4240-002 printed pages 191 to 194 and 007-4311-002 printed page 36: one router ASIC with eight NUMAlink 3 ports, an L1 controller, a USB hub, a power board and two fans; no processors, memory or I/O

components.name: SN1 router
components.notes: The part number is the public SN1 router family's; that it is the R-brick's fitted ASIC is inferred from the family and the shared software-reported router Revision 1, not measured. Zero chip inputs are an emulator configuration policy. Router-to-router links may use any port, the C-brick ports included, so only nodes are bound to ports 2 to 5.
sources: 007-4311-002 printed pages 36 and 37: eight ports, and a C-brick connects only to port 2, 3, 4 or 5, since only those carry the USB signals that reach its L1
007-4240-002 printed page 196: the C-bricks are cabled only to ports 2, 3, 4 and 5

machine.name: Origin 3400
machine.notes: An Origin 3400 of 16 processors drawn with one R-brick, as the technical configuration guide's 8- to 16-processor interconnect draws it: four four-processor C-bricks on router ports 2 to 5 and an I-brick on the first C-brick's XIO (II) connector at its XBridge port A. The bundles ship a second R-brick, which this composition does not show. The R-brick presents all eight ports: an Origin 3400 R-brick ships with two of them switched off, and which two and how is not established by any source this tree cites. The rack's L2 controller, which the guide requires beside an R-brick, is not modelled, nor is the R-brick's USB hub traffic to the C-brick L1s; running without them is a stated limitation, not a claim that the hardware does. Each C-brick is fitted as the Origin 3200's is, four 400 MHz R12000s with 8 MB secondary caches and 4096 MB in eight 512 MB banks; the bundles ship C-bricks without memory, so the memory is a model choice. The router answers the model's synthetic diagnostics, which no hardware record settles. The stock PROM's discovery prints one failed vector read and a bad link on each node before it finds the router; the cause is not diagnosed.
